Name: Chao Phraya Sky Park
Description: A landscaped pedestrian park built on the unfinished pillars of an abandoned 1980s skytrain bridge, crossing the river high above the water. From the middle you get open views of the river, Memorial Bridge and the Thonburi and Old Town skylines.

Name: Wat Chedi Luang
Description: The ruined 15th-century chedi of Wat Chedi Luang (once the tallest structure in Lanna, cracked by a 1545 earthquake) is floodlit at night and nearly empty after the tour groups leave. Next door, the all-teak hall of Wat Phan Tao glows with lanterns. Come in the afternoon first for the free monk chat tables on the grounds, then stay for dusk.

Name: Wat Phan Tao
Description: The ruined 15th-century chedi of Wat Chedi Luang (once the tallest structure in Lanna, cracked by a 1545 earthquake) is floodlit at night and nearly empty after the tour groups leave. Name: Baan Dam Museum (Black House)
Description: Three striking modern art temples: the all-white Wat Rong Khun with its mirror mosaics, the sapphire-and-gold Wat Rong Suea Ten, and Baan Dam (Black House), an eerie complex of dark teak buildings by artist Thawan Duchanee. Add the Saturday/Sunday walking streets or Singha Park tea fields if you stay over. Your note: exciting, but far. If i end up having on the higher end for number of days, I'll add. In general, worth adding to our final writeup in case I have extra time.

Name: Cheow Lan Lake (Khao Sok)
Description: An emerald reservoir inside one of the world's oldest rainforests, ringed by sheer limestone karsts. Sleep in a bamboo raft house on the water, kayak at dawn while gibbons call, swim off your porch, and hike to jungle caves such as Nam Talu.

Name: ICONSIAM (New Year countdown)
Description: Bangkok's biggest New Year celebration runs as a five-day festival at ICONSIAM's River Park with concerts and drone shows, ending with a 1,400 m fireworks display along the Chao Phraya at midnight on 31 December. Watch from the river park, a rooftop, a riverside hotel or a dinner cruise. Your note: great, but i get IN on the 1st, so not sure if thats too late for part of the festival

Name: Phra Nakhon Khiri (Khao Wang)
Description: Ride a cable car up Khao Wang to Phra Nakhon Khiri, King Rama IV's hilltop palace and temples with views over the town and paddies. Then visit Tham Khao Luang, a cave temple where sunbeams fall through the roof onto rows of Buddha images, and Wat Yai Suwannaram's Ayutthaya-era murals.

Name: Royal Barges National Museum
Description: A boat shed on the Bangkok Noi canal holding the gilded royal barges used in the rare Royal Barge Procession, including the 46 m Suphannahong with its swan-head prow. It's small but striking, and reaching it through a stilt-house lane by the canal is half the fun.

Name: Si Satchanalai Historical Park
Description: Thailand's first capital (13th–15th century), a UNESCO park of lotus ponds, lotus-bud chedis and serene walking Buddhas that you explore by bicycle. Its twin city Si Satchanalai, an hour north, is quieter still: overgrown temples like Wat Chang Lom ringed with elephant statues, where you may be the only visitor.

Name: Sukhothai Historical Park
Description: Thailand's first capital (13th–15th century), a UNESCO park of lotus ponds, lotus-bud chedis and serene walking Buddhas that you explore by bicycle. Its twin city Si Satchanalai, an hour north, is quieter still: overgrown temples like Wat Chang Lom ringed with elephant statues, where you may be the only visitor.

Name: Tham Khao Luang cave
Description: Ride a cable car up Khao Wang to Phra Nakhon Khiri, King Rama IV's hilltop palace and temples with views over the town and paddies. Then visit Tham Khao Luang, a cave temple where sunbeams fall through the roof onto rows of Buddha images, and Wat Yai Suwannaram's Ayutthaya-era murals.

Name: Wat Ban Den
Description: A sprawling hillside temple complex of dazzling Lanna-style halls, gilded roofs and 12 zodiac chedis, built over decades by a revered local abbot. Locals visit their birth-year chedi; you wander between ornate wooden and mirrored buildings with mountain views behind.

Name: Wat Ratchabophit
Description: A royal temple from 1869 where everything is covered in multicolored Chinese ceramic tiles, around a circular cloister and a gilded chedi. The ordination hall's doors are inlaid with mother-of-pearl, and the interior surprises with a Gothic, European-style chapel. Next door is a little-visited royal cemetery with Khmer, Gothic and Thai-style memorials.

Name: White Temple (Wat Rong Khun)
Description: Three striking modern art temples: the all-white Wat Rong Khun with its mirror mosaics, the sapphire-and-gold Wat Rong Suea Ten, and Baan Dam (Black House), an eerie complex of dark teak buildings by artist Thawan Duchanee. Name: Bridge over the River Kwai
Description: See the Bridge over the River Kwai, the moving Thailand–Burma Railway Centre and the Allied war cemetery, then ride the WWII 'Death Railway' train along the cliff-hugging Wang Pho (Tham Krasae) viaduct above the river. With an early start a driver can add Hellfire Pass or Erawan Falls. Your note: Interesting (want to know more), but have to weigh against other day trips

Name: Ko Kret
Description: A car-free island in the Chao Phraya, home to a Mon community known for terracotta pottery. Walk or cycle the 6 km loop past potteries, the leaning white chedi of Wat Poramai Yikawat and stalls selling Mon desserts and fried flowers.

Name: Krung Thep Aphiwat station (sleeper train north)
Description: Thailand's classic rail journey on the Chinese-built sleeper cars (in service since 2016): staff make up your bunk after dinner, and you wake to the train climbing through teak forests and the Khun Tan tunnel into the northern hills. Upgrade option: the restored 1960s 'Blue Jasmine' train (launched Nov 2025) runs a 9-day luxury Bangkok–Chiang Mai journey with stops at Ayutthaya, Uthai Thani and Sukhothai.

Name: Mon Cham
Description: A Hmong highland project on a ridge at ~1,400 m with flower and vegetable terraces, tent campsites and wide views over the Mae Sa valley. The drive up the winding Mae Sa road passes waterfalls and strawberry farms; sunrise brings a sea of mist on cold mornings.

Name: Phan Fa Leelard Pier (Saen Saep canal boat)
Description: The commuter canal express that roars along a narrow canal between Old Town and the modern centre; you pull a tarp up against splashes while passing stilt houses, mosques and high-rises. Ride from Phan Fa Lilat pier near the Golden Mount to Pratunam, then change for Asok.

Name: Phra Pathom Chedi
Description: Phra Pathom Chedi, at 120 m one of the tallest stupas in the world, marks where Buddhism may first have arrived in Thailand; walk its cloisters and terraces. Nearby, the peaceful Sanam Chandra Palace of King Rama VI mixes Thai and English-Tudor buildings in a huge park.

Name: Phra Prang Sam Yot (Lopburi monkeys)
Description: An ancient Khmer and Ayutthaya-era town centred on Phra Prang Sam Yot, three linked 13th-century laterite towers ruled by hundreds of macaques. Also see the large Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat ruins and King Narai's 17th-century palace, now a museum. Your note: dont think i would do this in addition to ayutthaya but curious to learn more especially about the monkeys

Name: Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden
Description: Thailand's leading botanic garden spread across forested hills, with a ~400 m canopy walkway about 20 m above the trees, glasshouses of orchids and lotus, and quiet trails. Views stretch over the Mae Sa valley and Doi Suthep range.

Name: Sanam Chandra Palace
Description: Phra Pathom Chedi, at 120 m one of the tallest stupas in the world, marks where Buddhism may first have arrived in Thailand; walk its cloisters and terraces. Nearby, the peaceful Sanam Chandra Palace of King Rama VI mixes Thai and English-Tudor buildings in a huge park.

Name: Talat Noi & Song Wat Road
Description: A maze of old Hokkien lanes full of car-parts workshops, street art, shrines and the 200-year-old So Heng Tai courtyard mansion, plus the Holy Rosary Church and riverside cafés. Continue up Song Wat Road, a row of restored shophouses with spice traders, coffee bars and galleries.

Name: Tham Krasae (Wang Pho Viaduct)
Description: See the Bridge over the River Kwai, the moving Thailand–Burma Railway Centre and the Allied war cemetery, then ride the WWII 'Death Railway' train along the cliff-hugging Wang Pho (Tham Krasae) viaduct above the river. With an early start a driver can add Hellfire Pass or Erawan Falls. Your note: Interesting (want to know more), but have to weigh against other day trips

Name: Wua Lai Saturday Walking Street
Description: The Saturday night market on the old silversmith street is smaller and more local than the famous Sunday market. Stalls sell food, crafts and silverwork, and Wat Sri Suphan glows silver at the end of the street.

Name: Ban Tawai woodcarving village
Description: A long-established crafts village of open workshops where carvers make Lanna-style wood carvings, furniture and lacquerware. Walk the lanes and watch the artisans at work; it pairs well with Wat Inthrawat nearby.

Name: Bang Krachao (Sri Nakhon Khuean Khan Park)
Description: A jungle-covered loop of the Chao Phraya where 2 m-wide raised concrete paths wind through mangroves, banana groves and stilt villages. Rent a bike at the pier, ride to Sri Nakhon Khuean Khan Park with its lake and birdwatching tower, and stop at canal-side cafés; on weekends visit Bang Nam Phueng floating market.

Name: Bang Pa-In Royal Palace
Description: A royal summer palace on a river island with an elegant Thai pavilion floating in a pond, a Chinese-style throne hall and European mansions in manicured gardens. Nearby, Wat Niwet Thammaprawat is a Buddhist temple built to look like a Gothic church, reached by a cable-pulled cart-ferry.

Name: Bangkokian Museum
Description: A family's 1930s wooden house and garden kept exactly as it was, showing how a middle-class Bangkok household lived before the high-rises. Rooms of furniture, records, kitchenware and photos, plus a doctor's surgery building, all in a shady garden off Charoen Krung.

Name: Bo Sang Umbrella Village
Description: Bo Sang is the home of hand-painted paper and cotton umbrellas; workshops show every step from bamboo frame to painting. During the festival the village street is hung with hundreds of umbrellas, with parades, crafts and a 'Miss Bo Sang' on bicycles holding umbrellas. Nearby San Kamphaeng has silk and celadon workshops and the MAIIAM contemporary art museum.

Name: Doi Mae Salong
Description: A mountaintop village founded by Chinese Kuomintang soldiers who fled Yunnan in 1949, now surrounded by oolong tea terraces. Drink tea at plantations like 101 Tea, eat Yunnanese noodles, walk the morning market with Akha and Lisu traders, and climb to the Princess Mother's chedi for the view.

Name: Huai Nam Dang (Doi Kiew Lom viewpoint)
Description: Doi Kiew Lom viewpoint at the park headquarters looks over rolling ridges toward Doi Luang Chiang Dao, and in the cool season the valleys fill with a sea of mist at dawn. On the way back, Pong Duet has boiling geysers and natural hot pools in the forest for a soak.

Name: Huay Tung Tao Lake
Description: A reservoir at the foot of Doi Suthep lined with bamboo huts on stilts where you lounge over the water and order grilled fish, som tam and cold drinks. Giant straw sculptures sit around the lake, and a paved loop is good for a bike ride or short walk.

Name: Museum Siam
Description: A modern, interactive museum in a grand colonial-era ministry building that asks 'what does it mean to be Thai?' through playful rooms on history, food, beliefs and identity. In 2026–27 it is also a Bangkok Art Biennale venue with contemporary installations.

Name: Nang Loeng Market
Description: Thailand's first land market (1900), a covered wooden market in an old community with stalls of traditional Thai desserts, curries over rice and noodles. Look for the century-old khanom thuai stall and the old cinema façade; nearby lanes are home to families of classical dancers and musicians.

Name: Phra Sumen Fort & Santi Chai Prakan Park
Description: A whitewashed 1783 octagonal fort, one of two survivors of the old city walls, stands in a small riverside park with views of the Rama VIII cable-stayed bridge. Locals jog and do aerobics at dusk, and Phra Athit Road behind it has old shophouses, bars with live music and small restaurants.

Name: Phu Chi Fa
Description: A knife-edge cliff at ~1,600 m jutting out toward Laos, where a sea of clouds fills the Mekong valley at dawn. A 20–30 minute walk from the village takes you to the point in the dark; you watch the sun rise over the clouds.

Name: Warorot Market
Description: Chiang Mai's main local market (Kad Luang): three floors of northern sausages, chili pastes, dried fruit, hill-tribe textiles and household goods. Across the street, Ton Lam Yai flower market is busiest at night with marigold garlands for the temples.

Name: Wat Inthrawat (Wat Ton Kwen)
Description: A small, carefully preserved 1850s Lanna temple in a village setting: a teak wihan with sweeping layered roofs and a rare open-sided pavilion (mondop) that once sheltered a Buddha relic during processions. It is regarded as one of the best examples of original Lanna wooden architecture left.

Name: Wat Phra That Lampang Luang
Description: Wat Phra That Lampang Luang is a walled 13th–15th-century hilltop temple, perhaps the finest surviving Lanna wooden temple, famous for a pinhole image of the chedi projected upside down in a dark hall. Lampang town has teak mansions like Baan Sao Nak, horse-drawn carriages and a Sunday walking street along the river.

Name: Wat Phumin, Nan
Description: A sleepy, old Lanna-era city in a green valley, famous for the 19th-century murals of Wat Phumin (including the 'whispering' couple) and the gold chedi of Wat Phra That Chae Haeng. Rent a scooter or hire a driver for the Sapan village rice terraces, the ancient Bo Kluea mountain salt wells and the sea-of-fog viewpoint at Doi Samer Dao.

Name: Wat Suthat & the Giant Swing
Description: One of Bangkok's six first-class royal temples, with a vast ordination hall, huge wall murals and the 8 m bronze Phra Si Sakyamuni Buddha brought from Sukhothai. Out front stands the red teak Giant Swing, once used in a Brahmin swinging ceremony, and the surrounding streets sell bronze Buddha images and monk supplies.

Name: Wiang Kum Kam
Description: The first capital of King Mengrai (late 1200s), abandoned after floods and buried under river silt until the 1980s. More than 20 excavated temple ruins sit among village lanes and rice fields; you explore by bicycle, horse cart or small tram, stopping at Wat Chedi Liam (a working temple with a stepped Mon-style chedi) and Wat Kan Thom.
